extracted.intended_audience: NLP researchers and practitioners working on Chinese humor datasets and LLM evaluation
extracted.subtask_description: Designing, curating, and evaluating a multi-task Chinese humor dataset (CFunSet) and training/evaluating a humor-specialized LLM (CFunModel) for tasks such as humor recognition, crosstalk response selection, joke/crosstalk generation, and joke explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Task diversity / sample structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Each sample in CFunSet consists of: Instruction (a description and prompt specifying the task type), Input (relevant data upon which the output should be based), Output (the expected response generated for the task).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design tasks to align with the data and include diverse formats (Humor Recognition, Crosstalk Response Selection, Joke Generation/Continuation, Crosstalk Generation/Continuation, Humor Explanation, etc.). Examples and sample structures are provided in Appendix/Table 6.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tieba–JokeBar selection criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Posts and comments collected from Tieba—JokeBar that contained more than 50 characters were selected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Joke Generation/Continuation tasks the first sentence of the selected joke is extracted as the Input. This selection threshold (>50 characters) is used to ensure sufficient content for task design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-joke validity filter
rubrics_metrics.description: Text must be a single joke with humor and contain no other elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filtering prompt used: '以下是一段文本，请判断它是否具有幽默感。符合条件的文本必须是单一的一条具有幽默性的笑话，并且没有任何其他的元素。只需要输出“符合条件”或“不符合条件”。文本如下：{文本}' (Output: '符合条件' or '不符合条件'). Use this to remove multi-item posts or non-joke content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic non-humor filtering using a model
rubrics_metrics.description: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct was employed to filter out non-humorous content, retaining only texts classified as jokes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use an LLM classifier with an explicit prompt to decide validity. This automated filter is part of the data cleaning pipeline but may need manual checks; known limitation: some misspellings/punctuation errors may remain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theme / keyword extraction
rubrics_metrics.description: Extract simple theme/keyword descriptions for jokes to support task design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt template: '用简单的词语描述概括这个笑话的主题/关键词，仅输出主题/关键词即可：{笑话}' / 'Use simple words to describe and summarize the theme/keyword of this joke. Output only the theme/keyword: {Joke}'. Extracted keywords are used to construct Joke Generation tasks (e.g., input: keyword/theme -> output: joke).

rubrics_metrics.name: CrossDial / Crosstalk Response Selection format
rubrics_metrics.description: Input: Crosstalk script segment and multiple-choice candidate responses; Output: select the most appropriate response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation metric: accuracy. Test sizes reported: 4,664 samples for Dougen response selection and 2,688 for Penggen response selection. Structure: source texts, multiple-choice options, target texts (Table 1 / CrossDial description).

rubrics_metrics.name: Humor Recognition task format and metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Input: a paragraph/text; Output: label indicating whether the text is humorous (Humorous / Not humorous).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accuracy is used to assess performance. HumorWB was split manually into 4,200 training and 1,091 testing samples for this purpose. Prompting must clearly define 'humorous' (e.g., linguistic techniques like puns, sarcasm, exaggeration, absurdity, unexpected logic).

rubrics_metrics.name: Humor Explanation (punchline explanation) task
rubrics_metrics.description: Input: a joke; Output: an explanation of the joke's punchline or the reason for its humor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chumor2.0 was used for this task (jokes and corresponding punchline explanations). The model is expected to provide accurate explanations of why a joke is funny; example prompts and outputs are provided in the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joke Generation / Continuation task (open-ended)
rubrics_metrics.description: Input: a keyword/theme or the first sentence of a joke; Output: the complete joke or continuation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open-ended generation tasks are evaluated by qualitative case study rather than automatic metrics like BLEU, which the paper states are insufficient for humor. Example: '我将给你笑话的第一句话，请你生成整个笑话。笑话的第一句话如下：' (I will give you the first sentence...).

rubrics_metrics.name: Crosstalk Generation / Continuation task (open-ended)
rubrics_metrics.description: Input: a crosstalk script segment (Dougen/Penggen style); Output: continuation/completion of the crosstalk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluated by qualitative case study to judge coherence and humor (examples shown in Table 5). Task emphasizes role dynamics (Dougen introduces topics; Penggen replies to enhance humor).

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of high-humor examples from prior corpora
rubrics_metrics.description: When incorporating CCL2019-Chinese-Humor-Computation data, human-written jokes from Task 1 and jokes labeled as 5 (the highest level of humor) from Task 2 were selected as inputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only high-quality/higher-labeled jokes from legacy datasets to ensure better training signals for generation tasks; keywords/themes from these were extracted using Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation metrics guidance: discrete vs open-ended
rubrics_metrics.description: Use accuracy for discrete classification/selection tasks (Humor Recognition, Crosstalk Response Selection); use qualitative case studies for open-ended generation tasks (Joke/Crosstalk Generation/Continuation) because automatic n-gram metrics are insufficient for humor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set evaluation temperature appropriately (paper: temperature=1 for baseline models during evaluation; CFunModel evaluation set temperature=0). For generation evaluation prefer human judgment and illustrative examples to assess humor, coherence, and role interplay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt structure for model training/inference
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a prompt structure combining Instruction and Input as described in dataset design (Instruction + Input).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent prompt format across tasks improves supervised fine-tuning alignment. Prompts shown in tables and examples (e.g., '生成一个主题为“中饭”的笑话。' -> generate a joke on the theme 'lunch').

rubrics_metrics.name: Supervised fine-tuning training configuration
rubrics_metrics.description: CFunModel SFT setup: base model Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct; trained for 2 epochs, learning rate 2e-5, batch size 128 on four A40 GPUs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set temperature to 0 during evaluation of the fine-tuned model to reduce sampling randomness. These hyperparameters are given as a recommended configuration for reproducing similar fine-tuning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data cleaning and quality limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Despite cleaning, some misspellings, grammatical errors, and incorrect punctuation may still remain in the final dataset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge residual noise when using web-collected data; consider additional normalization or manual curation if needed. The paper notes that automated filtering was applied but is not perfect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical and IP considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: All data sources used in this dataset are publicly available on the internet. Multiple techniques were used to eliminate inappropriate language, but some content may still inadvertently cause offense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When releasing or using the dataset, document provenance and content warnings; be transparent about filtering steps and residual risks of offensive content.
